name: Mt. Michelson, South Face
text: [overview] The southern side departs from the glacier of that name, covers 1000-2000' of loose blocks, talus and snow, and then follows a final line of snow and ice up to the crest of the summit ridge.
[detailed_rack] A few pickets and ice screws may help.
earlierWhy: why: Route leaves a glacier but the text does not say whether crevasses are met.
heldBecause: the page describes the peak's normal route, which may not be this face

lastPage.why: The normal route up the peak is listed as a glacier and snow climb starting from the south glacier.

name: West Ridge
text: [descent_text] From the summit, put on crampons and descend west on snow or ice until the scree slopes leading toward Twincicle Pass appear.
[descent_text] Go down through Twincicle Pass and the Twincicle Valley, which is a tangle of alders, and cross the short but very steep Twincicle Glacier.
earlierWhy: why: Descent crosses a short steep glacier.
heldBecause: the page names a short steep glacier on the descent but no crevasse or bergschrund hazard

lastPage.why: The normal descent crosses the named Twincicle Glacier, a short very steep one where the guide says to wear crampons.

name: Dana Couloir
text: [overview] Roughly 1,000 ft of 40-degree snow and ice, a friendly introduction to gully ice.
[what_to_bring] crampons and ice axe — needed early in the season
earlierWhy: why: A 40-degree snow and ice couloir; nearby Dana Glacier involvement is not settled.
heldBecause: the page names the small Dana Glacier but no crevasse or bergschrund hazard

lastPage.why: The approach goes up to Dana Glacier and the route page says to cross the glacier before the couloir.

name: Right Mendel Couloir
earlierWhy: why: Winter and spring snow and ice couloir; no glacier on the line. | secondReview: unsure/yes: Mendel has a small glacier under its north side and nothing describes the line.
heldBecause: the report names the small Mendel Glacier but no crevasse or bergschrund hazard

lastPage.why: A climber report describes crossing the Mendel Glacier to the face, then roped climbing in the couloir.

name: North Face
text: [overview] The climb crosses the glacier to a clear couloir centered on the north face, ascends it (about 40 degrees) until a solid rock cap stops it, then veers right onto gentler terrain, mostly 3rd class, to reach the flat top before the summit itself.
[approach] Descend a broad, low-angle scree chute, turn south and go up the recess, passing Snow Lakes, to reach the glacier under the north face.
earlierWhy: why: The text says the party crosses a glacier below the face, but it is a small Sierra glacier and its hazard is unclear.
heldBecause: the page names a small glacier below the face but no crevasse or bergschrund hazard

lastPage.why: The route page sends the party up the glacier below the face to the couloir, with crampons and axe.

name: Queen's Way
text: [overview] A route up Apache by way of the Isabelle Glacier, entering from the head of the South Saint Vrain valley.

[approach] From the Brainard Lake area start at the Long Lake trailhead and follow the Pawnee Pass trail past Long Lake to Lake Isabelle, then continue west along the Isabelle Glacier trail to the tarn below Navajo, Apache and Shoshoni peaks.
[approach] Cross the Isabelle Glacier to its southwest corner, where the route climbs a steep snow ramp to a saddle below the summit.
[approach] These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.
earlierWhy: why: Crosses the Isabelle Glacier then a steep snow ramp; crevasse hazard there is not settled.
heldBecause: the page names the small Isabelle Glacier but no crevasse or bergschrund hazard

lastPage.why: The route page has the party cross the Isabelle Glacier to its southwest corner before the snow ramp.

name: North Face
text: [what_to_bring] crampons and ice axe — early season
earlierWhy: why: Only an early-season crampons note; Vesper Glacier remnant nearby.
heldBecause: the report crosses the small Vesper Glacier and a moat but names no crevasse hazard

lastPage.why: The trip report has the party descend to the Vesper Glacier and traverse it to the face, with a moat to cross late season and crampons, axe and rope on the gear list.
